1_which_grant_admits.method: One 46-entry journal built entirely through the CLI, including two live grants over the same capability and scope, an effective revocation of the newer one, a second revoke:authority and its withdrawal, and one call of every other BUILT transition. Replayed with RecordService. For each COMMITTED receipt the live grant set was recomputed here at the position strictly before that receipt's own event, and the cited grant was compared against the last-in-append-order live grant sharing its node, operator, capability and scope. The operation's expected scope was never assumed; the comparison is against the cited grant's own four fields, so it holds without reading the service's scope table.

1_which_grant_admits.the_one_citation_that_is_not_the_newest: receipt seq 18, console.revoke. The newest live revoke:authority at that position was the grant being withdrawn, so the receipt cites the next-newest. That is the exclusion rule firing, observed rather than asserted, and it is the only departure from newest-wins in the whole journal.

two_writers.an_honest_qualification: in this reproduction the two failures co-occur exactly: 41 broken chains and 41 stale citations, and no trial produced one without the other. The row states them as two consequences of one window, which is consistent; but every stale citation I observed sits in a journal that is already unreadable, so I cannot attest a stale citation on an intact chain.
two_writers.chain_break: CONFIRMED. Design one, two ordinary processes on a fresh store across a stagger sweep: 5 of 120 trials left the journal unreadable with soveraeign_record_service.core.BrokenChain, all 5 at zero stagger (5 of 12). Both children exited 0 and printed a success record in every trial, broken ones included.
two_writers.citation_of_a_revoked_grant: CONFIRMED, which the prior observation could not reproduce. Design two widens the window rather than the odds: 120 padding entries are appended to the journal so each writer's reconstruct() takes longer, and the revoker is started first with the opener staggered into it. 41 of 80 trials produced a COMMITTED console.open-channel receipt citing a grant that a revocation strictly earlier in the same journal had already withdrawn, with both children exiting 0. The rate is stagger-dependent: 7 to 10 of 10 at -60 ms through 0 ms, and 0 of 10 at +10 ms or later, where the opener simply refuses.
two_writers.owed_elsewhere: the row routes this to the Record Service, and the source agrees: RecordService.append reads head() and commits in its own transaction, so nothing under services/console/ can close it.
two_writers.uncaught_traceback: CONFIRMED. Against a store whose chain is already broken, grants, open-channel and operations each exit 1 with zero bytes on stdout and a soveraeign_record_service.core.BrokenChain traceback on stderr. That is this CLI's own contract broken, and it is the one thing the module docstring says never happens.

a_malformed_invocation_answers_in_json.help: --help, -h and a subcommand --help print usage text at exit 0 with empty stderr. The _Parser docstring declares this on purpose. cli.py's own module docstring says exit 0 means committed and that every command writes one JSON object, so a machine caller sending --help gets a non-JSON answer at the success code. Small, and inside the concern.
a_malformed_invocation_answers_in_json.method: 73 invocations of the shipped CLI as a subprocess. Every required flag of every one of the 15 subcommands omitted one at a time (32 invocations), each subcommand with no flags at all (15), plus an unknown subcommand, no subcommand, empty argv, a value outside choices, the same choice in lower case, an unknown flag in both spellings, an unknown root flag, a flag wanting a value at the end of argv (three places), positional junk before and after the subcommand, three forms of bare double dash, an ambiguous abbreviation, an abbreviated subcommand, a flag given twice, a malformed --node, an empty string subcommand, a bare dash, root flags with no command, and a non-ASCII subcommand.
a_malformed_invocation_answers_in_json.the_three_that_were_not_usage_errors: a bare double dash before the subcommand, an unambiguous abbreviated flag (--read for --reader), and the same flag given twice. argparse accepts all three, so the CLI ran the operation and answered REFUSED at exit 2, which is correct. They are recorded because a machine caller that duplicates a flag gets the last value silently and one that abbreviates gets a match, and neither is declared anywhere.
a_malformed_invocation_answers_in_json.vacuous_case: there is no integer-typed argument in this CLI, so 'a non-integer where one is wanted' has nothing to attack. --root is type=Path, which accepts any string. The nearest reachable case, a flag wanting a value at the end of argv, answers USAGE_ERROR.
a_malformed_invocation_answers_in_json.witnessing_the_check: the committed cases for this repair - test_declared_refusals.AUsageErrorIsStillOneJsonObject and the missing-flag case in test_cli_walk - call cli.main in process with stdout and stderr redirected. That does read the real bytes argparse writes, so it is not a declaration; but no committed test drives a malformed invocation as a subprocess, and scripts/witness_console.py, which is the subprocess harness, does not cover usage errors. The 73-invocation run above is the first subprocess reading of this repair.
